headlines.title: 코스피-코스닥 ‘ 상장폐지 시총 기준 강화 ’ 6개월 늦춘다
headlines.summary: 시황 악화 등 반영 내년 7월로 유예 상폐돼도 요건 충족땐 ‘코넥스’ 이전 코스피가 107.73포인트(1.64%) 오른 6687.21에 장을 마감 마감한 4일 오후 서울 중구 하나은행 본점에서 딜러들이 업무를 보고 있다. 코스닥은 23.29포인트(2.95%) 오른 813.50에 마감, 원·달러 환율은 8.9원 내린 1350.4원에 마감했다. 2026.09.

headlines.title: '코스닥 퇴출강화' 6개월 유예 … 흑자기업은 코넥스 이전 허용
headlines.summary: 정부, 상장사 반발에 '속도조절' 시총기준 상향 내년 7월로 연기 정부가 부실기업 퇴출을 위해 코스닥 상장폐지 시가총액 기준을 높이려던 계획을 6개월 유예하기로 했다. 이에 따라 내년 1월이 아니라 7월부터 제도가 시행된다. 또 상장폐지에 따른 충격을 줄이기 위해 일정한 재무 요건을 충족한 기업은 정리매매 없이 코넥스 이전 상장을 허용한다.

headlines.summary: [코스닥 상폐 시총기준 강화 유예] 주가부양 위한 마지막 기회 부여 “시장충격 완화” “낙인효과 키워” 코넥스 이전 허용엔 반응 엇갈려 한국거래소 상장폐지 시가총액 기준을 300억 원 미만으로 높이는 조치가 내년 7월로 연기되면서 코스닥 상장사 약 200곳이 상당 기간 퇴출 부담을 덜게 됐다.

top5_headlines.title: 코스피-코스닥 ‘ 상장폐지 시총 기준 강화 ’ 6개월 늦춘다
top5_headlines.summary: 시황 악화 등 반영 내년 7월로 유예 상폐돼도 요건 충족땐 ‘코넥스’ 이전 코스피가 107.73포인트(1.64%) 오른 6687.21에 장을 마감 마감한 4일 오후 서울 중구 하나은행 본점에서 딜러들이 업무를 보고 있다. 코스닥은 23.29포인트(2.95%) 오른 813.50에 마감, 원·달러 환율은 8.9원 내린 1350.4원에 마감했다. 2026.09.

top5_headlines.title: '코스닥 퇴출강화' 6개월 유예 … 흑자기업은 코넥스 이전 허용
top5_headlines.summary: 정부, 상장사 반발에 '속도조절' 시총기준 상향 내년 7월로 연기 정부가 부실기업 퇴출을 위해 코스닥 상장폐지 시가총액 기준을 높이려던 계획을 6개월 유예하기로 했다. 이에 따라 내년 1월이 아니라 7월부터 제도가 시행된다. 또 상장폐지에 따른 충격을 줄이기 위해 일정한 재무 요건을 충족한 기업은 정리매매 없이 코넥스 이전 상장을 허용한다.

top5_headlines.title: 비상장주식 내년 2월부터 '토큰증권'으로 사고판다
top5_headlines.summary: 상장주식·채권·펀드로 확대 내년 2월부터 비상장주식과 기관투자가 대상 사모 사채·머니마켓펀드(MMF) 등을 토큰증권(STO)으로 거래할 수 있게 된다. 중장기적으로는 상장주식과 채권뿐 아니라 부동산, 미술품 등 실물자산도 토큰증권 형태로 투자할 수 있게 된다. 개인투자자에게는 그동안 접근하기 어려웠던 상품들을 더 빠르고 투명하게 거래할 길이 열릴 전망이다.

top5_headlines.title: [단독]경제교육 힘주는 재경부 … '국가경제재정교육원' 신설
top5_headlines.summary: /사진=(세종=뉴스1) 김기남 기자 재정경제부가 대국민 경제교육을 강화하고 직무교육을 체계화하기 위해 소속기관인 '국가경제재정교육원'(이하 교육원) 신설을 추진한다. 기존 경제교육과 직무교육에 더해 기후 위기·저출산 등 각 부처의 경제 정책과 연계한 융복합 교육까지 강화한다는 구상이다.

key_headlines.title: US Semiconductor Investment Discussions Formalized Between Korea and US
key_headlines.summary: The Blue House confirmed that semiconductor investment is included in official Korea-US discussions, with the US indicating that tariff avoidance requires investment commitments. The government plans to announce the first US-bound investment project soon.

key_headlines.title: KOSDAQ Delisting Criteria Strengthened by 6 Months
key_headlines.summary: The government postponed strengthening market capitalization requirements for KOSDAQ delistings from January to July 2027 due to market deterioration. Profitable companies meeting financial requirements will be allowed to transfer to KONEX without liquidation procedures.

key_headlines.title: Non-listed Stock Trading Begins via Security Tokens from February 2027
key_headlines.summary: Starting February 2027, non-listed stocks and institutional private bonds will be tradable as security tokens (STO), expanding to listed stocks, bonds, and real assets over time. This opens previously inaccessible investment products to retail investors.

key_headlines.title: Four US Companies to Invest 2.8 Trillion Won in Korea
key_headlines.summary: US semiconductor, advanced materials, and clean energy firms committed to 2 billion dollars in foreign direct investment to Korea across semiconductor materials, display technology, and offshore wind sectors.

key_headlines.title: Government Establishes National Economic and Fiscal Education Institute
key_headlines.summary: The Ministry of Economy and Finance plans to create a new institute to strengthen public economic education and systematize job training, including convergence education on climate crisis and low birth rates.

sections.Hot Economy News: Korea-US semiconductor investment discussions have been formally confirmed, with US officials emphasizing that tariff avoidance requires Korean investment commitments. The government announced plans to unveil the first US-bound investment project shortly. Simultaneously, regulatory changes are reshaping Korea's financial markets, with KOSDAQ delisting criteria postponed and security token trading set to launch in February 2027. These developments signal significant shifts in capital flow patterns and investment accessibility for retail investors.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: China is revising its national accounting system to better reflect AI and digital economy contributions to GDP, adjusting for lower growth rates through statistical methodology changes. The US Federal Reserve faces pressure from the Trump administration to cut rates at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting, with threats of trade restrictions against surplus countries if action is not taken. Korea's inflation remains a key policy consideration as the central bank evaluates its next rate decision amid rising consumer and producer prices.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSPI rose 1.6% to 6,687 points and KOSDAQ gained 2.95% to 813.50, supported by stabilizing US Treasury yields and strong New York market performance. Retail investors increased purchases of short-term US Treasury ETFs amid high-interest-rate concerns, seeking stable monthly dividend income while minimizing bond price volatility. Market analysts identify 5% on the 10-year US Treasury yield as a critical psychological threshold for potential stock market declines.
sections.Industry & Technology: US firms in semiconductors, advanced materials, and clean energy are committing 2 billion dollars in Korean investments, driven partly by tariff concerns. Korean companies including steelmakers and semiconductor producers are establishing direct manufacturing operations in the US to circumvent high tariffs, fundamentally reshaping supply chains. Chinese tech company Xiaomi showcased integrated ecosystem products from AI chips to electric vehicles and humanoid robots at IFA 2026, demonstrating vertical integration strategies across industries.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul Housing and Communities Corporation's long-term jeonse residents average 6 years and 9 months of occupancy, with 72% successfully purchasing homes upon exit; however, conversion to ownership sales remains prohibited. Apartment prices continue rising despite government tax reforms announced in early August, with Seoul's real estate market showing sustained upward momentum. Next week will see 2,852 housing units supplied across seven nationwide developments, including projects in Seoul's Wolgyeok and Seongnam's Bokjeong areas.
sections.International Economy: President Trump threatened to halt trade with countries running surpluses with the US if the Federal Reserve does not cut rates at the September FOMC meeting, applying extreme pressure on monetary policy. This unprecedented ultimatum targets countries like Korea and China, reflecting Trump's protectionist stance and demands for more favorable US trade balances. The threat underscores escalating trade tensions and economic nationalism shaping global commerce patterns.
sections.AI & Economy: Labor unions emphasize the need for shorter working hours and quality job creation alongside large-scale AI, semiconductor, and future vehicle investments in the Gwangju-Jeollanam region. Demand for drone and AI-big data specialists is rising as traditional document courier and administrative roles diminish, reflecting structural labor market transformation. South Korea shared its AI policies at the 32nd APEC Small and Medium Enterprise Ministers' Meeting in Guangzhou, while unions demand just AI transition and enhanced public services.
sections.Others: Specialized personnel in drone and AI-big data fields are experiencing increasing demand as administrative work automation progresses, with traditional paper document handling roles declining. Former US Forces Korea commander Brooks suggested possible US-North Korea talks between November and December 2026. The government issued guidelines clarifying holiday pay obligations for workers, potentially affecting employment contracts going forward, with compliance required for new or renewed contracts since May 29.
